Completeness and contamination of each bin, estimated with CheckM, and selection of the most complete bins for further analysis. Commands for this step were run in `checkm/`.

Check bin quality using checkm. First change directory to checkm.

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm

cat ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print length($seq),$name}' | sort -n
```

Found largest contig in the bbd assembly, it is contig_120 (must manually add this contig because it probably isn’t included in the bins from metabat).

Must save the contig_120 as a bin of its own, in the same folder as the metabat bins, so that all the later steps treat it just like the other bins. Then, must copy all of the bins, including the longest contig, into the bins_bbd folder inside checkm.

```{bash}
samtools faidx ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta contig_120 > ../metabat/bins_bbd/contig_120.fa
cp ../metabat/bins_bbd/*.fa bins_bbd/
```

Create slurm script for the checkm run. Save it within the checkm directory as run_checkm_bbd.sh

```{bash}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=60
#SBATCH --ntasks=6 --mem=40gb

echo "Starting checkm in $(pwd) at $(date)"

shopt -s expand_aliases
alias checkm='apptainer run -B /pvol/:/pvol /pvol/data/sif/checkm.sif checkm'

checkm lineage_wf bins_bbd out -t 6 -x fa -f checkm_results_bbd.txt

echo "Finished checkm in $(pwd) at $(date)"
```

Submit the checkm job: `sbatch run_checkm_bbd.sh`

## Functional analysis of the BBD Metagenome

The purpose of binning is to sort the metagenome into species and strain within the black band disease community. They can also be leveraged to make inferences about metabolic processes present within a BBD lesion. Overall, the purpose of this functional analysis is to investigate (1) what taxonomic groups of microbes are present, and (2) what can they do in terms of genes and biochemical pathways present.

Check results within checkm_results_bbd
```{bash}
head checkm_results_bbd.txt 
```

Marker lineage for top few bins: o__Cytophagales, p__Cyanobacteria, k__Bacteria, and  o__Clostridiales. 

Look further down the list:
```{bash}
head -n 20 checkm_results_bbd.txt 
```

The analysis will focus on the most complete bins, i.e bins with a completeness greater than 15% (more likely to contain the majority of useful information on function within the bbd community). These bins will probbaly represent the most abundant taxa (and best assembled). 

Extract top 15% bins for completeness:
```{bash}
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15'

cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}'

cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}' > bbd_topbins.txt
```

Saved output as bbd_topbins.txt.
